summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar in Tibetology who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford. He served as a Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and was a researcher at the CNRS (attested 2019).

Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under traditional teacher Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. Around 1929, he was a member of the Servants of the Buddha.

Indologist Somadeva Vasudeva completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. His positions include researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry, posts at Oxford (attested 2005), Kyoto University (Professor, 2011), and Columbia University (Assistant Professor of Sanskrit).

Somboon Watana specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and was an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) studied Buddhism at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1933–1941) under Vajirayanavangsa and Satyananda Puri. He led Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961), taught meditation at Kasetsart University (1976), and served as abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013).

Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master's Degree in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Sonam Chhoki works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Tibetology. She earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden is a researcher in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher at the University of Hamburg, where she also held a post as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Sonam Jamtsho works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he studied at the University of Hamburg as a Doctoral Local Researcher and held an appointment there as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter.

Sonam Kachru works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago under Daniel A. Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and the Max Planck Institute, later becoming Assistant Professor at Yale (attested 2026).

Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD (~1999–2002) at the University of Tasmania under mentors Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, subsequently holding a post there around 2003.

Sonam Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle. As of 2026, he is Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she holds the post of Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Songeun Choe works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Myung-dae Moon and doctoral studies under Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a Japanologist who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1979), completing her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under teachers Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch (born 1967) is a linguist who completed her Magister, doctorate, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1986–2005). She held posts at Heidelberg University Library, Erlangen-Nuremberg (2007), Vienna (visiting professor, 2008), and Munich (deputy professor, 2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under Hung Wu. She taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004) and held posts at Stanford and USC (attested 2010).

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich. He later held a post at Dongguk University.
Soorakkulame Pemarathana is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Saranindranath Tagore.
